# Reverse proxy and edge security

- Terminate TLS with current protocol defaults, valid certificates, HSTS where safe for the domain, and no disabled certificate verification to upstreams.
- Define trusted proxy hops and strip/replace client-supplied `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, identity, and authorization headers before adding trusted values.
- Never trust a proxy-set user/role header unless the application is unreachable except through the authenticating proxy and the proxy cryptographically verifies identity. Prefer a verifiable token with issuer/audience constraints.
- Default routes to deny and expose only intended hosts, paths, methods, and upstreams. Protect admin, metrics, health detail, debug, and management paths separately.
- Set request/header/body, buffering, timeout, rate/concurrency, and upstream response limits appropriate to each route. Reject ambiguous framing and conflicting length/transfer headers.
- Configure CORS, CSP, cache, redirects, and cookie rewriting deliberately; avoid origin reflection, open redirects, cache of authenticated content, and weakening secure cookie flags.
- Normalize/route paths consistently with the application. Prevent encoded traversal, alias/root confusion, unintended static files, backup files, and internal location bypass.
- Do not disclose server versions, internal hostnames, upstream errors, or default pages. Use generic external errors and protected redacted access/security logs.
- Store private keys and credentials outside committed config with restrictive permissions. Do not embed basic-auth passwords, tokens, or upstream secrets.
